To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the lattice QCD calculation of the nucleon electromagnetic form factors is in excellent agreement with experiment for Q2 < 1 GeV, and that this agreement is a consequence of the extrapolation to the chiral and continuum limits.

(i) the lattice data for the ratio GM/GE is consistent with experiment at all values of Q2, (ii) there is a strong indication that the lattice data for GE is in agreement with the experimental data for all values of Q 2, (iii) the lattice data is consistent with experiment for the ratio GE/GA at all values of the momentum transfer.

lattice QCD calculations are able to reproduce the form factors for the nucleon to a level of agreement that is comparable to that of phenomenological fits, but without the need for any additional free parameters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the calculation of the electromagnetic and axial form factors of the proton and neutron from first principles.
the calculation of the electromagnetic form factors of the proton and neutron using the lattice technique.
the calculation of the nucleon electromagnetic form factors using lattice QCD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lattice QCD results are in excellent agreement with the experimental data, for all of the form factor ratios, over the entire range of momentum transfer.
lattice QCD is now in a position to provide a quantitative understanding of the nucleon electromagnetic form factors.
lattice QCD is now a reliable tool to provide guidance for the interpretation of the experimental data on the nucleon form factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for Q2<1 GeV2 and for all the form factors, we have a clear understanding of the systematic errors and a reliable procedure for extrapolation to the chiral regime.
the lattice QCD results are in good agreement with the data, and that the lattice results are in agreement with the results of the chiral extrapolations.
the lattice QCD data are consistent with a picture of the nucleon where the electric charge is distributed in a manner similar to the magnetic moment and that the ratio GE/GA is close to unity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the form factors are remarkably well-behaved and the chiral extrapolation is remarkably smooth.
the chiral extrapolation of form factor data is a well defined problem, and one that is amenable to lattice QCD.

the form factor data are already sufficiently accurate that the lattice QCD calculations are beginning to constrain the form factor data, and that the data are now sufficiently precise that they are starting to reveal the underlying physics.
